$comment: Request-shape contract v1 — the full matrix across every official provider. Each case feeds the same metadata and user intent into every runtime request builder. endpointPath, headers, query params, body includes/excludes lock the upstream wire shape. If the catalog's profile table or transport output changes, update this fixture and all platform harnesses in the same change. metadata.profiles is a byte-for-byte copy of the profile table the catalog serves, and the copy is exhaustive **both ways**: nothing served may be missing here, and nothing may appear here that is not served (gem_contract_conflict_web is the one explicit exception, as a Conflict canary). Every profile in the reasoning/webSearch/imageGen groups must additionally be driven end to end by at least one case, so a profile no client can actually execute cannot sit here unnoticed. The suites that enforce all of this are web/packages/core/src/providers/request-builders/__tests__/request-shape-contract.test.ts, ios/Oriveo/OriveoTests/RequestShapeContractTests.swift and android/app/src/test/java/ai/oriveo/community/core/provider/RequestShapeContractTest.kt. v1 does not assert fallback, responseAdapter or moonshotMaxToolLoops; each client covers those in its own tests. The numeric evidence behind these decisions comes from direct measurement (61 probes) rather than from reading model names. The generation outbound surface is covered by an additive key that older consumers can ignore: metadata.profiles.generation is copied byte for byte from the generation group of the catalog's profile table; every official providerKind has at least one intent.generationOverrides case, asserting that the value the user set appears in the real body a production builder produces, using the upstream field name from template.wire (bodyExcludes locks, in the other direction, that a canonical parameter id is never sent out verbatim); generationProviderKindUniverse × generationOutboundExemptions is a structural gate — every providerKind in the full set either has an outbound case or is on the exemption list with a reason.

gem_contract_conflict_web.$comment: Conflict canary: webSearch writes generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel=LOW; Gemini 3 reasoning profile must win with HIGH. tools array remains a normal web-search merge. This is the one profile this fixture allows to exist only here and not in the catalog's profile table — it isn't a real upstream shape, but a deliberately constructed same-key conflict between reasoning and webSearch, used to lock down the merge priority across all clients. It is identified by the 'Conflict canary' prefix on this $comment, which is what exempts it from the both-ways correspondence above; every other profile must match the catalog's table exactly.

grok-4.5.$comment: grok's defaultTransport is unified to openai_responses across the family (the search_parameters field on /chat/completions now returns 410); 4.5's reasoning legacy profile is therefore the Responses-shaped grok_effort_responses and its generation template is openai_responses. No model is assigned to grok_effort_45.

cases.$comment: caseId is stable API for the three client suites and must not be renamed. grok-3-mini goes through /v1/responses (the same shape as grok.responses.web_reasoning.deep: the legacy oai_chat profile still sends a top-level reasoning_effort on the Responses body).

expect.$comment: The oai_responses profile does not send summary:"auto", and none of the three clients injects it on the direct BYOK path. The evidence: o4-mini with reasoning:{effort:"medium",summary:"auto"} returns 400 "Your organization must be verified to generate reasoning summaries"; the same request without summary returns 200. Note that the relay path deliberately **keeps** summary and is unrelated to this case (this case covers the official BYOK direct path only).
oai_responses has no defaultLevel, so automatic means literally zero injection: the whole reasoning object stays out of the body.

gpt-5.2 and above add one more tier, xhigh (measured: gpt-5.4-mini high averages 1507 tokens vs xhigh 8674, with no overlap across five runs). gpt-5 / 5.1 / the o-series return 400 not supported for it, so this must be its own profile rather than an extra tier added to oai_responses.

A regression lock: gpt-5.2-pro / 5.4-pro / 5.5-pro measurably reject effort=low with a 400, so oai_responses_pro declares no fast tier. Selecting "fast" must be clamped by all three clients down to automatic (below balanced there is only automatic) — meaning zero injection and falling back to the upstream default — and must never send effort=low.
The gpt-image family rejects response_format (measured: 400 Unknown parameter); requestDefaults only sends size+n. No client may hardcode response_format again.

All three clients dispatch Grok image generation through the imageGen profile's route=images_api. requestDefaults authoritatively sends {n,response_format}; size is forbidden (measured on xAI: 400 Argument not supported: size).

ant_adaptive (the sonnet-4.6 family) differs from ant_adaptive_max only in not having a max tier; both request shapes use thinking.type=adaptive + output_config.effort, and must never fall back to ant_budget's thinking.budget_tokens (the adaptive family rejects it upstream).

This tier is the only difference between gem_level and gem_level_flash: on the pro family, a hard problem measurably separates MEDIUM and HIGH (4964 vs 10886 tokens, p=0.0122), while on the flash family the difference is not significant (p=0.8345), so flash declares no balanced. Losing this case would make it impossible to tell whether the two profiles got swapped.

gemma only accepts thinkingLevel's minimal/high tiers (lowercase), and rejects thinkingBudget and LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH. The tier mapping is fast→minimal / deep→high, with no balanced/max. Sending gem_budget or gem_level by mistake causes a live 400 on gemini BYOK.
gemini 1.5's older web search uses googleSearchRetrieval + dynamic_retrieval_config, a different wire shape from 2.0+'s google_search; sending google_search to it returns a 400 upstream.

cases.$comment: caseId is stable API for the three client suites; grok-4.5 goes through /v1/responses + grok_effort_responses (reasoning.effort), and the chat-shaped reasoning_effort must never be sent for it anymore.

expect.$comment: Together image generation is dispatched uniformly through route. Missing this branch sends all image-generation models to /chat/completions, which returns a 400 upstream ("Image inference is not supported on this endpoint. Please use /images/generations instead"). requestDefaults authoritatively sends {size,n} (measured against every image model with a 200 response and a data[0].url).

The together_images_no_n variant: same endpoint, same route, just without n (measured: 400 {"param":"n","message":"n is not supported for this model"}; dropping n and sending only size returns 200). Clients must always expand requestDefaults as-is and never add n themselves.

The openai_responses template: max_output_tokens keeps its name, verbosity nests under text.verbosity. bodyExcludes locks the rule that a canonical parameter id must never be sent out verbatim — passing the id straight through instead of looking it up in the wire table is exactly the kind of silent drift this guards against.

The anthropic_messages template renames two fields: max_output_tokens→max_tokens, stop→stop_sequences. max_tokens=512 also locks in that an explicit user value overrides the default the builder would otherwise write from metadata's maxOutputTokens.
The gemini_generate_content template nests everything under generationConfig.*; none of the same-named top-level fields may appear, or generateContent returns a 400 immediately.

Regression lock: route_require_parameters must never be presented as editable unless the value actually goes out. It is the one setting the catalog publishes for openRouter alone, with the wire nested at provider.require_parameters.

cases.$comment: caseId is stable API for the three client suites; grok-4.5 goes through the openai_responses generation template: max_output_tokens keeps its name on the wire, and max_tokens must never appear.

generationOutboundExemptions.reason: relay's generation profile does not come from /api/metadata; it is synthesized locally on-device from engineProfile/transport (relayGenerationProfile in web/apps/app/lib/core/chat/stream-options.ts, LocalEngineContract on iOS and Android). This fixture's metadata.providers only describes what the catalog sends down, so adding a fake relay provider entry here would be fabricating catalog output. relay's outbound injection is covered separately by the relay case in generation_parameter_contract.v1.json.
